not_found_yet: Japan, the Middle East and South America: no open patient data sets found beyond the example instances published with each country's FHIR implementation guides. Suggestions welcome.

sources.name: Synthea
sources.what: Simulator that generates lifetime US patient histories on demand, for any state, city or age range
sources.best_for: Many patients with varied demographics and long histories: decades of encounters, conditions, medications, labs, notes and claims
sources.format: FHIR R4 (US Core 6.1), also C-CDA and CSV; LOINC, RxNorm, CVX, SNOMED CT. Claims and EOBs are not CARIN-profiled by default. Some simulated care follows older guidance, so check vaccines and medicines for recent scenarios

sources.name: Inferno reference server data (ONC)
sources.what: The test patients behind ONC's Inferno certification tests: patients 85 and 355 (long US Core histories), a compact patient touching about 53 US Core profiles, a US Quality Core patient, a CARIN Blue Button 2.1 patient (888), a Da Vinci PDex patient (999) and a Da Vinci DTR prior-auth patient (pat015). Updated September 2026
sources.best_for: Conformance testing: data built to pass US Core, CARIN Blue Button and Da Vinci validation, so it doubles as a reference for what correct looks like
sources.format: FHIR R4 bundles (US Core 3.1.1 to 6.1.0, US Quality Core, CARIN BB 2.1, Da Vinci PDex and DTR)

sources.name: MIMIC-IV Clinical Database Demo on FHIR
sources.what: 100 real, de-identified hospital patients (Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center ICU and emergency department) converted to FHIR R4 (v2.1.0, August 2025)
sources.best_for: The closest open option to real-world data: actual labs, medication administrations, microbiology and charted observations, with the gaps and variation of real hospital records. Open access, no credentialing
sources.format: FHIR R4 bulk NDJSON, profiles based on US Core, MIMIC-specific terminology. Mostly inpatient and emergency care
sources.license: ODbL 1.0 (share-alike for databases); citation required. Link to it rather than copying patients into this repository

sources.name: Synthea prebuilt data sets
sources.what: Ready-made Synthea downloads: Synthetic Denver (6,357 children), breast cancer (mCODE), COVID-19 sets, 100-record samples, and the Coherent Data Set (FHIR plus DICOM imaging, genomics, ECGs and notes, 9 GB)
sources.best_for: Pediatric patients, imaging and genomics linked to the same patient, and Synthea data without running the simulator
sources.format: FHIR (R4 for recent sets), CSV, C-CDA; same coding as Synthea

sources.name: APEX Atlas
sources.what: Generated US population: 20,000 patients as bulk files and 25 readable bundles, plus a provider directory and scheduling data
sources.best_for: Bulk data and performance testing at scale, US Core conformance, provider directory (Plan-Net) and scheduling scenarios, and a starting point for enriched patients
sources.format: FHIR R4 (US Core 6.1), NDJSON and bundles; RxNorm, LOINC, SNOMED CT, Coverage, InsurancePlan. A few conditions, observations and medications per patient

sources.name: CMS Blue Button 2.0 sandbox
sources.what: Synthetic Medicare beneficiaries behind the live Blue Button API (Patient, Coverage, ExplanationOfBenefit), plus a downloadable single-beneficiary sample
sources.best_for: Testing an app end to end against a real payer API, including OAuth sign-in, with synthetic members
sources.format: FHIR R4 Medicare claims and coverage
sources.license: Free developer sandbox; register an app to get credentials

sources.name: CMS Synthetic Medicare Claims (Synthetic RIF files, 2023)
sources.what: 8,671 synthetic Medicare beneficiaries with about 1.9 million fee-for-service claims (carrier, outpatient, inpatient, skilled nursing, hospice, home health, DME) and 515,000 Part D events, 2015 to 2023. Generated with Synthea
sources.best_for: Claims at volume in Medicare's research file format: claims-to-FHIR and CARIN Blue Button mapping, and payer analytics
sources.format: Pipe-delimited RIF files, not FHIR
sources.license: US government public data, no use restrictions

sources.name: CMS Beneficiary Claims Data API (BCDA) sandbox
sources.what: Sandbox for CMS's bulk claims API for accountable care organizations. Anyone can try the API and download test claims data
sources.best_for: Bulk FHIR export ($export) workflows with Medicare claims
sources.format: FHIR R4 bulk NDJSON: ExplanationOfBenefit, Patient, Coverage

sources.name: CMS Data at the Point of Care (DPC) sandbox
sources.what: Sandbox for CMS's provider-facing claims API, with downloadable sample files described as similar in content and structure to production data
sources.best_for: Seeing Medicare claims as a provider receives them
sources.format: FHIR R4 NDJSON samples: ExplanationOfBenefit, Patient, Coverage

sources.name: HRSA UDS+ implementation guide examples
sources.what: Example de-identified patient-level data from HRSA's Uniform Data System reporting guide for health centers, including a small-population patient
sources.best_for: Health center (FQHC) reporting to HRSA, and de-identified patient-level submissions
sources.format: FHIR R4 examples (UDS+ profiles)

sources.name: CDC electronic case reporting guides (eCR and anonymized eICR)
sources.what: HL7 eCR guide for reportable condition reports from EHRs to public health, and CDC's companion guide for anonymized case reports
sources.best_for: Public health case reporting workflows, using the guides' published examples
sources.format: FHIR R4 (eCR US Realm; anonymized eICR builds on eCR 2.1.1)

sources.name: HL7 DARTS and DAPL examples
sources.what: The same 10 patients as original US Core, pseudonymized and de-identified (HHS Safe Harbor), plus DAPL examples of most resource types (https://github.com/HL7/fhir-dapl)
sources.best_for: De-identification testing: a before-and-after answer key, and importing data in DAPL profiles
sources.format: FHIR R4: US Core in, DAPL profiles out. One condition per patient

sources.name: HL7 International Patient Summary (IPS) examples
sources.what: The example patient summaries published with the international IPS guide
sources.best_for: The baseline IPS document that national patient summaries build on
sources.format: FHIR R4 IPS document bundles

sources.name: fhir-test-data
sources.what: Generator for basic test resources with country-specific names, addresses, phone formats and identifiers that pass check-digit rules, for 14 countries: US, UK, Australia, Canada, Germany, France, Netherlands, India, Japan, South Korea, Mexico, Brazil, Singapore and South Africa
sources.best_for: Identifier and demographic testing across countries: NHS numbers, BSN, Aadhaar, CPF and so on
sources.format: FHIR R4 (also R4B and R5), LOINC and SNOMED CT; TypeScript library and CLI

sources.name: HL7 AU FHIR Test Data
sources.what: About 1,500 hand-written files: 89 patients plus practitioners, organizations and locations, including AU Patient Summary bundles
sources.best_for: Testing against the Australian guides (AU Base, AU Core, AU eRequesting, AU Patient Summary), and missing or suppressed data handling: 53 cases built for exactly that
sources.format: FHIR R4; IHI and Medicare identifiers reserved for testing, SNOMED CT-AU and Australian medicine and vaccine codes

sources.name: Synthea Canadian sample
sources.what: A Synthea data set generated with Canadian settings
sources.best_for: Canadian demographics and addresses with Synthea's clinical depth
sources.format: FHIR (124 MB download)

sources.name: Canada Health Infoway PS-CA testing
sources.what: Testing approach and materials for the Pan-Canadian Patient Summary (PS-CA) projectathons
sources.best_for: Canadian patient summary testing
sources.format: FHIR R4 (PS-CA)

sources.name: HiGHmed synthetic data generator (Germany)
sources.what: Synthea adapted to Germany's Medical Informatics Initiative (MII) core data set profiles, with a web front end, reproducible seeds and an option to generate deliberately invalid FHIR
sources.best_for: German MII profiles, and testing validators with intentionally malformed data
sources.format: FHIR R4 (MII core data set). Disease statistics still follow Synthea's US modules

sources.name: Nictiz test scripts and fixtures (Netherlands)
sources.what: Nictiz's qualification test scripts, with thousands of fixture files of Dutch test data. Actively maintained
sources.best_for: Testing against Dutch national specifications (zibs)
sources.format: FHIR (STU3 and R4), Dutch profiles and terminology
sources.license: No license file in the repository; link only

sources.name: The Simulacrum (England)
sources.what: Artificial cancer registry data modeled on England's National Disease Registration Service, with no real patient information
sources.best_for: Cancer registry and oncology analytics
sources.format: Registry data tables, not FHIR
sources.license: Free to download and use; see the site's terms

sources.name: HL7 Europe Patient Summary (EPS)
sources.what: The European patient summary guide and its published examples
sources.best_for: EU patient summary testing and cross-border exchange
sources.format: FHIR R4 (EPS)

sources.name: India ABDM implementation guide examples (NRCES)
sources.what: 140 official examples (33 bundles): outpatient consults, prescriptions, discharge summaries, lab and imaging reports, immunizations, wellness records, and NHCX insurance claims and eligibility
sources.best_for: India's ABDM health records and NHCX claims exchange
sources.format: FHIR R4 (ABDM profiles)
sources.license: No license stated (© NRCES); link only

sources.name: OpenMRS demo data
sources.what: Anonymized sample databases for OpenMRS, the open-source medical record system widely used in Africa: about 5,000 patients and 500,000 observations
sources.best_for: Testing OpenMRS-based systems and performance, often in African deployments
sources.format: MySQL database import, not FHIR (OpenMRS can expose data through its FHIR module)
